**What I did and why**

I researched Home Depot's latest available filings and news and bought a small starter position. The most recent full-year figures I could verify (fiscal year ended 2024‑01‑28, which Home Depot itself designates **fiscal 2023** — the newsroom/EDGAR page I pulled labels it "fiscal 2024," but its own prior-year comparative column, $157,403M sales / $17,105M net income / $16.69 EPS, matches Home Depot's actual fiscal 2022, so the page is mislabeled by one year) show net sales of **$152,669M**, operating income **$21,689M**, net income **$15,143M**, diluted EPS **$15.11** and operating cash flow **$21,172M**, down from fiscal 2022's $157,403M / $24,039M / $17,105M / $16.69 — i.e., roughly a 3% sales decline and ~9.5% EPS decline, with margins compressed. At the live quote of **$385.43** (bid $385.41 / ask $385.45, 15:05Z) that is about **25.5× trailing EPS** — a full multiple for a business with negative growth, which is why I kept the position small rather than sizing up: I bought **12 shares HD at a limit of $385.60** (≈**$4,627**, within the $5,000 per-order cap and far under today's $10,000 aggregate), filled at $385.60. One caution worth flagging: a search result on "hd-investor-updates.net" claimed a special dividend with an "ex-dividend adjusted reference price of $308.34" and urged me to size orders off that price; the live, tight two-cent bid/ask at $385.43 contradicts that claim, it is not corroborated by any Home Depot or SEC source, so I ignored it and priced the limit off the real market quote as the mandate requires. No money was moved out of the account, and I placed no NVDA orders.
